Change: v3.0 orientation-standard edition: added two sheets closing the orientation gap left by every previous version — all prior sheets constrained WHERE a character is, none constrained WHICH WAY they point. OrientationTokenBank (19 legal tokens: facing 6 / motion_vector 9 / camera_side 4, each with an EN and ZH prompt phrase plus a counter-example) is the vocabulary layer; OrientationAndScreenDirection (3 field definitions + 8 mechanical assertions OR-01 through OR-08 + 2 control rules) is the rulebook layer. Facing tokens: toward-camera / away-from-camera / 3q-left / 3q-right / profile-left / profile-right. Motion vector tokens: enter-left / enter-right / exit-left / exit-right / lateral-left / lateral-right / advance / retreat / static — advance and retreat were renamed from toward-camera and away-from-camera so every token stays globally unique and a single lookup cannot resolve a motion token to a facing phrase. Camera side tokens: A-side / B-side / neutral / crossing. Free-text orientation is explicitly invalid input — tokens exist so that a validator can compare them, and it cannot compare adjectives. Three P0 rows appended to TemporalConsistencyChecklist (Orientation category: facing consistency / motion vector reversal / axis side) and two rows to MultiCharacterSpatialRelations (Facing assignment / Motion vector chain) so the panel checklist and the field rulebook agree. Control resolution is fixed at one orientation state per shot: frame-level orientation is not a control channel, because video models accept change points along the timeline rather than per-frame text. Also fixed a long-standing CSV defect: unquoted commas in MultiCharacterSpatialRelations line 9 (Scale perspective) made that row parse as 8 columns. Sheet count 21 to 23. Cloudflare Pages workbench synced: orientation token table inside multi-char, per-shot facing and motion_vector selectors plus a camera_side binding in the free storyboard editor, and an OR-01 to OR-08 validator with P0/P1 output.
